### Observed differences

- Participation in the three activities A19, A20 and A25 collapsed: in the earlier window each ran exactly once per trace (never repeated) in about 33, 29 and 40 in 100 traces respectively (65, 57 and 81 of 200 traces), while in the later window each appears in only 1 of 200 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- In the earlier window these three were mutually exclusive alternatives whose shares together cover essentially every trace, so a typical case executed exactly one of them; in the later window about 99 in 100 traces contain none of the three. [REL001, REL002, REL006]
- The block was embedded between A27/A28 and A29: whenever one of A19, A20 or A25 ran, it co-occurred with A27, A28 and A29, always after A27 and before A29, and A28 led into one of the three in about half of its outgoing transitions (roughly 16–19 in 100 to each). In the later window these relations are gone, with about 99 in 100 traces containing only A27, A28 and A29 of this group. [REL003, REL005, REL007, REL009, REL010, REL012, DIR006]
- Routing concentrated accordingly: A28 now leads almost exclusively to A29 (about 97 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, against about 43 in 100 earlier), and A27 now leads almost exclusively to A28 (about 98 in 100, against about 52 in 100 earlier, when it also led directly to A25, A19 and A20, together about 44 in 100). [DIR005, DIR006]
- Distances shrank by about one step: A27 to A29 is now typically 2 positions apart (about 96 in 100) versus typically 3 earlier (about 90 in 100); A28 to A29 is now almost always immediately consecutive (about 96 in 100) versus typically 2 steps apart earlier (about 52 in 100); A27 to A28 is now almost always directly consecutive (about 99 in 100 versus 52 in 100). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG004]
- Separately, the outgoing transitions of A10 were redistributed: earlier they concentrated on A15 (about 20 in 100), A47 (17), A16 (17) and A45 (14); later they spread over roughly twenty successors, the largest being A26 (17), A45 (15), and A16 and A41 (9 each). [DIR001]
- Minor shifts: A27's mean relative position moved slightly later (about 0.46 to 0.48) and A29's slightly earlier (about 0.57 to 0.55); both activities still occur in every trace in both windows. [POS004, POS005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the alternative block formed by A19, A20 and A25 — executed in the earlier window in essentially every case, exactly one of the three per trace, always after A27 and before A29 and closely tied to A28 — is no longer executed in the later window, so that cases now proceed from A28 directly to A29. Screening produced 30 qualifying items (all control-flow) where roughly 0.56 would be expected without a change, so the pattern as a whole cannot be explained by chance sampling. The support is direct and consistent: the participation drop rests on 57–81 traces per activity falling to 1, the relational items show the same three activities moving from exclusive alternatives embedded between A27/A28 and A29 to joint absence, the routing items show A27 and A28 concentrating onto A28 and A29 respectively, and the lag items show the A27→A29 and A28→A29 gaps closing by about one step. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL001, REL005, REL012, DIR005, DIR006, LAG002, LAG004]

An important competing explanation remains: the evidence cannot distinguish complete removal of the block from it being skipped in almost all cases, since each of the three activities still appears in one later trace and zero participation only means they were not observed. In addition, the later routing profiles of A19, A20 and A25 rest on a single trace each, so the apparent new successors (A38, A37, A31) are not reliable evidence about where these activities now lead. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]

Other differences: the redistribution of A10's outgoing transitions described above, which the evidence does not connect to the vanished block [DIR001]; and the small opposite position shifts of A27 and A29, which are based on event positions rather than clock time [POS004, POS005].

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- Two windows: 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 113 units tested, 30 items qualified, 0.56 expected by chance. All in control_flow family. So 30 items vs 0.56 expected — that's many times larger than chance expectation. This is a strong signal that something changed (the count cannot be explained by chance as a whole).

Evidence items:

OCC001: A19 participation dropped from 0.325 (65/200 traces) to 0.005 (1/200). Mean occurrences per trace 0.325 → 0.005. Recurrence 0 in both.

OCC002: A20 participation 0.285 (57/200) → 0.005 (1/200).

OCC003: A25 participation 0.405 (81/200) → 0.005 (1/200).

So A19, A20, A25 were each present in roughly 30-40% of traces before, and essentially disappeared in the after window (1 trace each out of 200).

DIR001: A10 outgoing transitions redistributed. Before: A15 0.20, A47 0.17, A16 0.17, A45 0.14, A21 0.086, A30 0.057, A28 0.029, A40 0.029, A13 0.029, A09 0.029, A23 0.029, A38 0.029. After: many components, A26 0.17, A45 0.15, A16 0.094, A41 0.094, A47 0.057, A15 0.057, etc. Support before 35, after 53. This is a redistribution of outgoing transitions from A10 — quite diffuse. Cosine dissimilarity 0.44.

DIR002: A19 outgoing: before A29 0.55, A28 0.42, A24 0.015, A20 0.015; after: A38 1.0. But support after = 1 (only 1 trace contains A19 in the after window). So this is based on 1 observation — weak. The after profile is essentially from a single trace.

DIR003: A20 outgoing: before A29 0.61, A28 0.375, A10 0.018; after A37 1.0. Support after = 1. Weak.

DIR004: A25 outgoing: before A28 0.51, A29 0.44, small others; after A31 1.0. Support after = 1. Weak.

DIR005: A27 outgoing: before A28 0.52, A25 0.20, A19 0.13, A20 0.10, small others; after A28 0.975, small others. Support 202/202. So A27 now goes almost always to A28, whereas before it went to A28 about half the time and to A25/A19/A20 the rest. Since A19, A20, A25 disappeared, A27's transitions to them disappeared too. Observed change 0.107, strength 0.995.

DIR006: A28 outgoing: before A29 0.43, A25 0.19, A19 0.18, A20 0.16, small others; after A29 0.97, small others. Support 204/200. So A28 now goes almost always to A29; before it also went to A25, A19, A20. Again consistent with A19/A20/A25 disappearing.

POS001: A19 position: support 0.325 → 0.005. Mean position ~0.52 → 0.49 (based on 1 trace). Weak after.

POS002: A20 position: support 0.285 → 0.005; mean 0.52 → 0.74 (1 trace). Weak.

POS003: A25: support 0.405 → 0.005; mean 0.51 → 0.69 (1 trace). Weak.

POS004: A27 position: support 1.0 both; mean 0.463 → 0.478, small shift. Observed change 0.019. Strength 0.995. Small but consistent shift later slightly.

POS005: A29 position: support 1.0 both; mean 0.570 → 0.549, small shift earlier. Observed change 0.021.

REL001: A19 & A20: before A_only 0.32, B_only 0.28, neither 0.395, cooccurrence 0.005; after neither 0.99. So both essentially disappeared; they were alternatives (rarely co-occurring) before, now neither occurs.

REL002: A19 & A25: similar — before A_only 0.32, B_only 0.40, neither 0.275; after neither 0.99.

REL003: A19 & A27: before cooccurrence 0.325 (A19 always co-occurs with A27, B_only 0.675), B_before_A 0.325; after B_only 0.995, cooccurrence 0.005. So A19 always appeared together with A27 before (A27 before A19), now A19 gone.

REL004: A19 & A28: before cooccurrence 0.325, B_before_A 0.19, A_before_B 0.13; after B_only 0.995. A19 always with A28 before, now gone.

REL005: A19 & A29: before cooccurrence 0.325, A_before_B 0.32 (A19 before A29); after B_only 0.995.

REL006: A20 & A25: before A_only 0.28, B_only 0.40, neither 0.315; after neither 0.99.

REL007: A20 & A27: before cooccurrence 0.285, B_before_A 0.28; after B_only 0.995.

REL008: A20 & A28: before cooccurrence 0.285, mixed order; after B_only 0.995.

REL009: A20 & A29: before cooccurrence 0.285, A_before_B 0.265; after B_only 0.995.

REL010: A25 & A27: before cooccurrence 0.405, B_before_A 0.40; after B_only 0.995.

REL011: A25 & A28: before cooccurrence 0.405, mixed; after B_only 0.995.

LAG001: A27→A28 lag: before lag 1: 0.52, lag 2: 0.45, lag 3: 0.017; after lag 1: 0.985, lag 2: 0.015. So A27→A28 became almost always immediately adjacent (lag 1), whereas before it was lag 1 or 2. Support 200/200.

Wait, let me think. Before: A27→A28 lag 1 (52%) or lag 2 (45%). A27→A29 lag 3 (90%). After: A27→A28 lag 1 (98.5%), A27→A29 lag 2 (95.5%).

If after A28→A29 is lag 1 (DIR006: A28→A29 0.97), then A27→A29 = 1+1 = 2. Consistent.

These activities sat between A28 and A29 (A28 → A19/A20/A25 → A29). In the after window, A19, A20, A25 essentially disappeared (1/200 traces each), A28 now goes directly to A29 (97%), and the A27→A29 lag shrank from 3 to 2, A28→A29 lag from ~2 to 1.

So the hypothesis: a block/branch consisting of A19, A20, A25 (an alternative set of activities executed between A28 and A29 in about a third of cases) was removed/skipped in the later window; the process now goes directly from A28 to A29.

Wait — but is it "removed" or "no longer taken"? The participation of A19/A20/A25 dropped from ~30-40% to ~0.5%. Zero participation only means not observed. The behaviour: these activities were optional/alternative and are now essentially not executed.
